status: PROTOTYPE. Not approved. Reported (untested, unverified) laptop facts: Windows 10 Pro, Python 3.11.9; build and bitness unknown.

windows.required: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit (finding only; Windows 10 support ended 2025-10-14 per Microsoft)

python.required: CPython 3.11.x, 64-bit, with venv and ensurepip; real interpreter (not the Microsoft Store alias)
python.why_minor: Hashed lock file exists only for cp311 (and cp313, not approved). Project tested on 3.11.

download.name: Python 3.11.9 Windows installer (64-bit)
download.blocker: python.org publishes only MD5 (weak) plus GPG/Sigstore signatures for this file. No official SHA-256 exists on the release page or the ftp index. A SHA-256 must not be invented. A preparer must verify the signature and then record a locally computed SHA-256, under a separate approval. Not done here; nothing was downloaded.
download.known_limits: 3.11.9 is the last 3.11 release with a Windows installer; no later security fixes are available as installers.

database.required: A database program on this PC identified as PostgreSQL 16.x (finding only). Any other or unidentified database-like program stays unknown; existing software is not permission to use it, to add a second one, or to start a service.

download.name: PostgreSQL 16.16-2 Windows x64 installer (EDB)
download.blocker: The sidecar was read (text only) from get.enterprisedb.com, the same host as the installer, so it detects corruption, not a compromised host. The installer file URL, file size and the vendor page's own 'Checksum for Windows' link target were not confirmed by me. A GitHub comment attributed to EDB staff describes signing and checksums; its author is unverified and nothing here relies on it. A second independent confirmation is needed before this value is treated as a pin. The version is also an owner decision (laptop PostgreSQL state is unknown).

wheels.required: Offline dependency folder: 44 wheels, every one listed in wheels.sha256, hash-matching, and present in the lock file (requirements-win-cp311.lock.txt)

download.name: Python dependency wheels (win_amd64, cp311)
download.source: https://pypi.org/ (via make_wheelhouse.sh on a preparer machine, never on the laptop)
download.pinned_by: option_b/requirements-win-cp311.lock.txt (== versions with sha256 hashes; pip --require-hashes)
download.blocker: The hashes are the ones PyPI served when the lock was made. They detect corruption and swaps after that point; they are not an independent publisher signature.

source.required: Project source of the reviewed commit 0bc929d (app/main.py present)

approved_exact_versions._note: Empty on purpose: approval of any version is an owner decision. A version that meets the rule is only a finding.
